units.text: Choose E F S Bursting for occasional peaks, not for a workload that must stay above baseline. Standard-class storage sets the baseline. When metered activity is below that baseline, the file system can accumulate burst credits.

During a peak, the workload can draw credits to reach higher throughput within its burst limits. If credits run low, sustained throughput returns to its baseline and applicable limits. Track the balance and compare against actual workload demand.

Reads and writes are metered differently, so do not equate every byte of client traffic with an equal charge against metered throughput. If the workload repeatedly exhausts credits, compare Elastic or Provisioned throughput.

Use E F S replication for a recovery copy, not instant failover. The source first synchronizes to the destination. That initial copy depends on the dataset and file count. Afterward, changes replicate asynchronously.

Use time since last sync to watch how far behind the most recent successful sync is. After the initial sync, E F S maintains a fifteen-minute recovery point objective for most file systems, with documented exceptions. It is not a promise that every newest write is present.

A recovery point objective is how much recent data you can afford to lose. The recovery time objective is how quickly you need service back. In a drill, make the destination writable as appropriate, verify mount targets, D N S, I A M and key access, then remount and test the application.

Decouple File Gateway writes from cloud processing. An N F S or S M B client writes through the gateway cache. The gateway uploads the file to S three asynchronously. Closing the local file alone does not prove the S three upload has finished.

Start processing after a completed object upload or a supported gateway upload notification. In this example Lambda transforms the object and writes processed data back to S three. Athena or Redshift Spectrum can then query the supported dataset.

Replicate the output to another bucket or Region only if the design needs it and the replication prerequisites are met. Replication does not coordinate multiple File Gateway writers or make processing synchronous.
Use one authoritative writer for an object set. Site A writes through its gateway into a common S three bucket. Sites B and C read from that same bucket using read-only gateway shares.
If objects change outside a reader's gateway cache, use RefreshCache as appropriate to update its object inventory. Refreshing the inventory does not download every object's contents in advance.
Shared S three storage does not provide distributed file locking between gateways. Keep the reader shares read-only, refresh when needed, and verify the client can see the expected version.

Make backup files recoverable by preserving versions first, then choosing how to tier and protect them. The backup application writes through File Gateway to S three. Lifecycle may move eligible versions to cheaper storage, but retrieval times and charges differ by class.

Object Lock protects eligible object versions; it does not stop a writer from creating a new version. During recovery, restore the selected version in S three, including any required archive restore, then refresh the gateway cache.
Validate the recovered file from the client. A retained version or successful cache refresh is not enough if the application cannot read and use the expected backup.

Restore with the interface the workload uses. For Volume Gateway, select the cloud snapshot recovery point and create an E B S volume for the E C two application when that is the recovery target. Verify the volume and application's data.

For Tape Gateway, retrieve the archived virtual tape and use compatible backup software to restore the files from that tape. The recovery path is a virtual tape library, not an E B S block-volume restore.
Local data that has not yet uploaded may be lost if the local gateway fails. Confirm the latest recovery point on the cloud side and test the right recovery procedure before an outage.

Choose F S X for Lustre Intelligent-Tiering when a parallel file workload needs elastic storage and only part of the dataset stays hot. Provision throughput separately. Add the optional S S D read cache when measurements show that frequently read data benefits from lower latency.

The file system automatically tiers less active data from Frequent Access to Infrequent Access and then to Archive Instant Access. Reading colder data can move it back to Frequent Access. This is a Lustre file system, not an S three archive-restore workflow.

The data is replicated across Availability Zones for durability. That does not prove that your clients will stay connected in an outage. Test client access, measure representative performance, and verify your separate recovery plan.

Choose Amazon E B S when an E C two instance needs a persistent block device. The operating system sees a disk for its boot volume, application data, or a database. Size the volume and its performance for the workload.

An E B S volume attaches within its Availability Zone. Use a snapshot to create a recovery volume elsewhere when needed. Multi-Attach is a specialized exception, not a replacement for a shared N F S or S M B file system.
Choose Amazon E F S when several Linux clients need the same files. The clients reach mount targets over N F S, and applications share a Pah-zicks file tree instead of attaching the same block disk.

Regional E F S stores data across Availability Zones; One Zone keeps it in one. Plan network reachability and file permissions in either case. If the requirement is a native Windows S M B share, choose a file service designed for S M B instead.

Choose an Amazon F S X family by protocol and workload. Windows File Server provides S M B and Active Directory integration. Lustre serves parallel workloads such as high-performance computing and machine learning.

For shared N F S, S M B, or eye scuzzy support, consider NetApp On Tap. For N F S with Z F S snapshots and clones, consider Open Z F S. The exam distinction is to choose the required file semantics first, then compare the family's performance and recovery options.
